## Verdict

missing

## Bearer

MainRacePageScreen — app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/race/MainRacePageScreen.kt

## Trigger

Composing MainRacePageScreen for a RUN segment with no reference race loaded and no sensor reading received yet — observed (composition runs on every `uiState` emission, from the screen's own collection of `viewModel.uiState`).

## Today

`MainRacePageScreen` renders four items behind `?.let`/`text?.let` guards: `uiState.stationLabel` (line 65), the top block's text (`TopBlockText`, line 122), the center block's text (`CenterBlockText`, line 145) and `sensorText(uiState.heartRate)` (line 85). `sensorText` (line 178) returns `null` for `SensorValueDisplay.Fallback`, for both the heart-rate item and the RUN center's `Pace` text. On a RUN segment with `referenceRace == null` and no distance/heart-rate sample yet, `MainRacePageViewModel.computeState()` (`MainRacePageViewModel.kt:304-329`) sets `stationLabel = null` (line 305, unconditionally for every RUN, not only when data is missing — a RUN has no station name coded at all), `top = RaceTopBlock.Hidden` (line 306-307), and `center = RaceCenterBlock.Pace(SensorValueDisplay.Fallback, TrendArrow.None)` (line 328). Every guard is skipped and the `ScalingLazyColumn` composes with zero items, over `DesignTokens.Color.screenBlack`: a fully black screen. A race starts at segment 1, which `SegmentBlueprint.typeAt(1)` always resolves to `SegmentType.RUN`, so this is the state every race begins in.

## Expected

`MainRacePageScreen` never composes with zero rendered items: every combination of `uiState` values produces at least a segment name and the two sensor blocks in their fallback shape.

Two further changes this fix cannot avoid, neither of which the screen alone can supply:

- `MainRacePageViewModel.computeState()`'s RUN branch (`MainRacePageViewModel.kt:304-305`) currently hardcodes `stationLabel = null` for every RUN. It must instead call `WatchStringResources.segmentName(index)` — the same call already used, unconditionally, in the `STATION`/`FINAL` branch (line 331) and already correct for `SegmentType.RUN` (`WatchStringResources.kt:126-127`, returning `segment_name_run` with the run number). Nothing today calls `segmentName(index)` on a RUN index; the value the screen would need to always render the station label does not exist on that path.
- `sensorText` (`MainRacePageScreen.kt:178-182`) is one function shared by the heart-rate item and the RUN center's pace item, both rendering nothing for `SensorValueDisplay.Fallback`. The two call sites need different fallback text — pace renders `—:—` followed by its unit, heart rate renders `—` — so `sensorText` cannot stay one function returning one fallback string; it needs a fallback text per caller, or one parameter carrying it. Neither the `—:—` pace fallback text nor a unit suffix on the pace value exists anywhere in `MainRacePageScreen.kt` or `DisplayFormatter` today (`DisplayFormatter.formatPace` returns a bare `m:ss`, never with a unit, in every state, not only `Fallback`) — the unit has to be added at the pace call site for every state, not only the fallback one, since `Expected` bars a fallback that reads differently from a real value's own shape. `DesignTokens.ZoneArc` (`app-wear/.../ui/theme/DesignTokens.kt:140-165`) declares an idle-opacity token (`arcOpacityIdleDim`) but no zone arc is composed anywhere in `MainRacePageScreen.kt` today — the screen renders the heart-rate value as plain colored `Text`, never an arc. Attenuating "the zone arc" as the gap describes has no existing arc component on this screen to attenuate; it does not exist and needs building, or the gap's fix needs restating against what this screen actually renders (a colored text, not an arc).
